artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the planar rational system of difference equations
  x_{n+1} = (α₁ + β₁ x_n + γ₁ y_n) / (A₁ + B₁ x_n + C₁ y_n),
  y_{n+1} = (α₂ + β₂ x_n + γ₂ y_n) / (A₂ + B₂ x_n + C₂ y_n),
where all parameters α_i, β_i, γ_i, A_i, B_i, C_i (i = 1, 2) are nonnegative real numbers, the initial conditions (x₀, y₀) are nonnegative, and the parameters are chosen so that both denominators remain strictly positive for every n ≥ 0.

By a "special case" of this system we mean a choice of which of the twelve parameters are zero and which are positive (with the convention that any positive parameter may be normalized, e.g. to 1, by rescaling), yielding finitely many distinct parameter patterns that give rise to genuinely different rational systems.

An equilibrium of the system is a point (x̄, ȳ) ∈ [0, ∞)² satisfying x̄ = (α₁ + β₁ x̄ + γ₁ ȳ)/(A₁ + B₁ x̄ + C₁ ȳ) and ȳ = (α₂ + β₂ x̄ + γ₂ ȳ)/(A₂ + B₂ x̄ + C₂ ȳ). The equilibrium is called locally asymptotically stable if it is Lyapunov stable and attracting on some neighborhood, and a global attractor (relative to the set of admissible initial conditions) if every admissible solution converges to it.

Problem: Determine exactly the set of special cases of the above system for which the following implication holds at every equilibrium:
  local asymptotic stability of the equilibrium  ⟹  global attractivity of the equilibrium
on the full set of nonnegative initial conditions yielding positive denominators for all n.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of characterizing all special cases of planar rational systems with nonnegative parameters for which local asymptotic stability implies global attractivity is a standing open problem in the theory of rational difference equations, going back to work of Camouzis and Ladas. Subsequent literature treats specific subcases (e.g., competitive or anticompetitive subclasses) but a complete characterization across all special cases has not been established.

status_evidence.title: When does local asymptotic stability imply global attractivity in rational equations?
status_evidence.snippet: Camouzis & Ladas, J. Difference Equ. Appl. 12 (2006), 863–885, posing and partially addressing this implication for rational equations.
status_evidence.claim: The implication LAS ⟹ GA for rational equations is a recognized research theme with only partial results.

status_evidence.title: Global Dynamics of Three Anticompetitive Systems of Difference Equations in the Plane
status_evidence.snippet: Studies specific subcases of the planar rational system, indicating the global classification remains incomplete.
status_evidence.claim: Only specific special cases of the planar rational system have been resolved in the literature.
